title: Electromagnetic Waves
standard_code: Grade 9, Quarter 1: Force, Motion, and Energy
standard_text: The electromagnetic spectrum; the speed, frequency and wavelength of electromagnetic waves; uses and harmful effects of each type of radiation. (summary of the MATATAG Science curriculum, Grade 9, Quarter 1: Force, Motion, and Energy)
meta_desc: Free Grade 9 Science worksheets (MATATAG, Quarter 1: Force, Motion, and Energy): the electromagnetic spectrum, speed, frequency and wavelength, order and uses of EM waves, photons and uses and dangers. 100 questions with answers.
key_sub: E = hf: higher frequency means more energy.
body_html:
How to think about it

Electromagnetic waves are made of electric and magnetic fields at right angles; they need no medium. In order of increasing frequency: radio, microwaves, infrared, visible light, ultraviolet, X-rays and gamma rays.

Light also behaves as particles called photons. The energy of one photon is E = hf, where h = 6.63 × 10⁻³⁴ J·s. Ultraviolet, X-rays and gamma rays have enough energy to damage cells, so exposure must be limited.

Example

Which has more energy per photon, UV or infrared?

E = hf

Answer: ultraviolet

Example

f = 6 × 10¹⁴ Hz. Wavelength?

λ = c/f

Answer: 5 × 10⁻⁷ m

Common mistakes

  • Thinking radio waves are sound waves.
  • Thinking all EM waves have the same frequency.
  • Thinking longer wavelength means more energy.
